issues.claim: Код и сообщение статуса gRPC передаются в trailers (`grpc-status`, `grpc-message`), а HTTP-статус ответа обычно `200`; ... Trailers-Only ... HTTP-статус всё равно `200`
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the error-handling page does not mention trailers, `grpc-status`/`grpc-message`, or an HTTP 200 status. It only covers status codes, RpcException and EnableDetailedErrors. The Trailers-Only sentence comes from the gRPC over HTTP/2 spec, which is not cited. From my own knowledge the facts are correct, but no cited source shows them, and option a is a core correct answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a third link to the gRPC over HTTP/2 spec (https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md, lang en, kind spec) with linkTitles in ru and en, or drop the Trailers-Only sentence and rely only on the cited pages.

issues.problem: The excerpt is cut off before the rich error handling section, so it does not show `grpc-status-details-bin`, `google.rpc.Status` or the Metadata constructor. I believe both claims are true, but the item's evidence does not support them.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the RpcException API page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/grpc.core.rpcexception) or the rich-error section of the error-handling page. issues.problem: The cited page says only that thrown exception types other than RpcException cause an UNKNOWN status. The wording "any exception" is slightly absolute, since cancellation handling may differ. The conclusion (no automatic KeyNotFoundException to NotFound mapping) is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "Other unhandled exceptions become `Unknown` with a generic message." in both locales.

issues.claim: Сообщение по RFC 6455 может состоять из нескольких кадров ... Закрытие в WebSocket - это рукопожатие: одна сторона отправляет кадр `Close`, другая отвечает своим
issues.problem: The RFC 6455 excerpt shows only the IANA opcode tables and the "Using the WebSocket Protocol from Other Specifications" section. It does not show fragmentation or the closing handshake. The fetch was also redirected to the info page. From my own knowledge (sections 5.4 and 7) the claims are true, but the item's evidence does not support them.
issues.suggestedFix: Link the specific sections (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455#section-5.4 for fragmentation and #section-7 for closing), or add the System.Net.WebSockets.WebSocket API page as a source and have the claims rest on it.

issues.claim: `ReceiveAsync` in .NET is not tied to frames at all: it fills the given buffer with whatever has arrived
issues.problem: This is imprecise. A single ReceiveAsync returns at most the remaining payload of the current frame and never spans two frames, so it is partly tied to frames. The practical conclusion that only EndOfMessage marks a message boundary is correct. The ru text has the same issue.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: "one `ReceiveAsync` returns at most the data of one frame and no more than the buffer size, so a message can need many calls; only `EndOfMessage` marks its end." Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: что из `WebSocketReceiveResult` говорит о конце сообщения?
issues.problem: The hint points straight at the `EndOfMessage` property, which is the core of the reference answer. The en hint has the same issue.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it: "Is one `ReceiveAsync` call always one whole message? What does a client wait for after it sends a Close frame?"

issues.claim: A single `WebSocket` allows one `ReceiveAsync` and one `SendAsync` at the same time
